newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's top pork producing state to export to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's top pork producing state to export to Japan.

text.p: Hog farmers in Mexico's Jalisco state will ship their first exports to Japan on July 19, an industry leader said on Wednesday.
The pork exports will be the start of a weekly shipment of at least 1,100 hogs to Japan, President of Jalisco's Hog Farmers Union Ricardo Jimenez Rubio told Reuters.
"Initially we are making a shipment of 1,100 hogs per week. In the short term this will increase to 2,000 hogs per week, in about two more months," Jimenez said.
Jalisco produces about 200,000 hogs per month and in 1996 produced 179,330 tonnes of pork carcass, about 20.03 percent of Mexico's total output.
Sonora state already has a history of exporting pork to Japan, but only special cuts. Jalisco, Mexico's largest hog producing state, will send frozen pork parts to Japan.

"Taiwan had been one of the principal pork exporters to Japan, but it made them sick and they stopped selling (to Japan)," Jimenez said. He explained that the Mexican exports would substitute exports from Taiwan and some from Denmark.
He said the state's hog farmers could later be able to export to Korea, Taiwan and Singapore.
Jimenez added that by November he expected Jalisco to be declared free of classic pork fever. No case of the fever has been identified in the past five years, he said.
Once the state is officially declared free of the disease, Jalisco will be eligible to export pork to the U.S. market.
